C-PLATFORM-UNTRUSTED-FEATURE-HOST-202609.Summary: Provide the ordinary execution boundary for user and AI-generated functionality: immutable WASM Components running in an OS-restricted feature-host process with explicit capability invocation imports, opaque handles, finite resources, and no ambient operating-system authority.
C-PLATFORM-UNTRUSTED-FEATURE-HOST-202609.Problem: The current WASM host proves import denial and resource limits but its WIT world exposes state and event operations rather than the browser-capability invocation model needed by programmable features. Native supervision terminates process trees but does not prevent same-account filesystem, network, process, or credential access. Treating either mechanism as a complete sandbox would make Worldline a local RCE surface.

Goals.Goal: Define a versioned feature ABI that can invoke admitted Worldline capabilities through host-issued opaque handles.
Run ordinary generated features in a separate OS-restricted host with deny-by-default filesystem, network, process, environment, device, and credential access.
Separate build sandbox, package validation, and runtime execution so generated source never executes with user-profile authority during compilation.
Enforce memory, CPU, wall-time, host-call concurrency, payload, rate, and storage quotas per runtime and installation.
Contain trap, panic, protocol violation, infinite loop, and host-call flood to the offending runtime.

Constraints.Constraint: SPEC APPROVAL DOES NOT APPROVE A PLAN OR IMPLEMENTATION.

The vNext architecture and effect-fence changes must be applied, and the durable package activation contract must be approved, before this change is planned; no untrusted feature may be activated until durable package activation is applied.
Ordinary user or AI-generated native binaries are not an allowed feature format.
WASM is an execution format, not authority; every privileged host import requires a valid runtime-scoped handle and broker admission.
No full WASI world, inherited environment, user profile, ambient network, arbitrary filesystem path, raw socket, process spawn, dynamic library load, or device access is exposed by default.
Manifest requested permissions are data and never self-grant authority.
Raw Grant, Principal, filesystem path, engine pointer, credential, or host object cannot cross the guest boundary.
Windows Job Object cleanup alone cannot satisfy the OS isolation criterion.
Feature failure must not terminate the kernel, engine, protected UI, updater, or recovery launcher.

NonGoals.NonGoal: Supporting arbitrary native plugins as untrusted code.
Giving generated code shell, compiler, package-manager, or debugger access at runtime.
Proving every possible WASM component correct.
Replacing kernel authorization with sandbox policy.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: A versioned feature WIT world exposes bounded capability invocation, state access, event observation, cancellation, and typed outcomes without exposing kernel internals.
Capability handles are host-issued, runtime and session scoped, attenuated, non-persistent, revocable, and checked again through the effect fence at privileged sinks.

An untrusted feature-host process runs under measured OS restrictions that deny ordinary access to the user profile, arbitrary files, outbound network, process creation, environment secrets, credentials, and privileged device APIs.
The build sandbox has no browser profile, credentials, installation authority, or automatic activation right and outputs an immutable package candidate.

Malicious fixtures prove denied filesystem, network, environment, process, handle forgery, cross-runtime handle use, oversized payload, memory exhaustion, fuel exhaustion, wall-time, and host-call flood behavior.
Trap, panic, protocol violation, or quota exhaustion terminates or resets only the offending runtime and removes its publications, subscriptions, leases, and handles.
A feature restart receives a new RuntimeId and handle table while retaining only explicitly installation-owned state.
Native system providers require separate provenance and trust admission and are never selected merely because a package asks for NativeProcess mode.
Non-Windows builds preserve the logical contract and report explicit unavailable isolation profiles until equivalent OS evidence exists.
Metrics and crash reports contain package/runtime identity, quotas, and failure class but exclude guest payloads, page content, secrets, and state values.

VerificationIntent.ExpectedEvidence: Fresh malicious-feature and OS-boundary evidence proves default-deny host resources, capability-only effects, finite quotas, new runtime identity after restart, and survival of trusted browser and recovery processes.

Assumptions.Assumption: Wasmtime Component Model remains the selected portable guest runtime and can be hosted inside a separately restricted process.
A Windows isolation primitive stronger than Job Object cleanup is available without disabling required Wasmtime execution; the plan must spike and record the chosen profile.
Build tooling can run in a separate disposable workspace without access to the active browser profile.
